answer: The economy grants one credential per capacity lease. An applicant reserves 3 GiB for 24 days and locks 90 credits; a spiral beacon requests two random chunks daily. An opal accumulator records one-use proof nullifiers, while a harbor contract binds the lease, payout address, and key. Six of eight established auditors must reproduce sampled proofs before voting power activates. Every extra identity therefore needs separate storage, bandwidth, locked capital, and a new quorum; missing or copied proofs slash 75%, and leases, samples, nullifiers, and penalties are public.
